messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: api-gateway-edge: elevated 502/504 rate detected. Alert threshold breached (errors > 5% over 1m). Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat; regions: us-east-1 primary, some spill to eu-west-1. Alert details: https://alerts.internal/alert/AGW-502-spike-2098765432
ops-oncall: Acked. I'm on it, switching to incident thread.
kevin: Oncall here — what's the customer impact? Any high-traffic clients?
sara: Looking at dashboards now. 5xx rate peaked at ~18% for the gateway cluster in us-east-1, p95 latency for /v1/generate up to 2.1s. Traffic is normal-ish, spike started ~2098765400 (≈5m ago).
prashant: Logs show repeated upstream failures: "upstream prematurely closed connection" and "read timeout". Samples: ```[ERROR] 502 from upstream: connection reset by peer
[ERROR] 504 upstream read timeout after 30s``` Looks like an upstream worker flapping or overloaded ml-pool-3.
sara: Rolling error heatmap: majority of 502s trace to node pool ml-serving-3 and envoy upstream host 10.40.12.7.
infra-ryan: Running quick health checks on gateway pods: `kubectl get pods -n gateway --selector=app=api-gateway -o wide`
infra-ryan: ```NAME                          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
api-gateway-6b7f9d58c7-2rlqg  1/2     Running   5          12d
api-gateway-6b7f9d58c7-kmh9z  2/2     Running   0          6d
api-gateway-6b7f9d58c7-ptx2m  1/2     CrashLoop 7          3h```
ops-oncall: CrashLoop on one gateway pod with high restart count — could explain partial capacity loss. Observed memory OOMs around same time in kubelet logs.
kevin: Any recent deploys to gateway or ml-serving? Deploy bot?
incident-bot: deploy-bot: deploy to ml-serving-3 completed 20m ago by prashant (sha: abcd1234) for quantization rollout.
prashant: I pushed a small quantized model to ml-serving-3 ~20m ago, but not to gateway. The ml-serving instances are showing higher CPU and longer GC. Possibly the new model variant increased latency and triggered upstream timeouts.
support-jess: Support queue: multiple customers reporting 502s on /v1/generate; high-severity tickets from two enterprise customers. Need ETA for mitigation to send update.
sara: Mitigation plan proposal:
• Shift traffic away from ml-serving-3 (disable routing to that pool)
• Scale gateway replicas temporarily to absorb retries
• Enable per-route circuit breaker for /v1/generate to fail fast for unhealthy upstreams
• Roll back quantized model on ml-serving-3 if routing shift fails

kevin: Agree. Execute in that order. Ryan/prashant, can you take routing and scale? I'll coordinate comms and fallback rules.
prashant: Starting traffic drain for ml-serving-3: `rlsctl pool set-weight ml-serving-3 0 --dry-run` then apply.
prashant: Applied: `rlsctl pool set-weight ml-serving-3 0` — routing change propagated to edge within ~20s.
infra-ryan: Scaling gateway: `kubectl scale deployment api-gateway -n gateway --replicas=12` — current desired was 6.
infra-ryan: Scale command accepted, new pods coming up.
kevin: Enable temporary retries/backoff in the edge config for clients with idempotent tokens and bump retry cap to 2. Also add stricter 502/504 fallback so we return 503 to clients for that route (to avoid cascade).
ops-oncall: Applying envoy config snippet for circuit breaker on /v1/generate: ```routes:
  - name: generate
    match: /v1/generate
    circuit_breakers:
      max_connections: 100
      max_pending_requests: 50
      max_requests: 200
```
ops-oncall: Config pushed to gateways — envoys accepted and reloaded.
sara: Metrics update: error rate dropped from 18% -> 4% within 90s after routing and CBs. p95 latency falling back to ~400ms.
support-jess: Notifying affected customers with interim status: sending 30-min update noting mitigation and ETA for full resolution.
prashant: ml-serving-3 healthchecks show GC pressure and ephemeral OOMs on a subset of instances. I'm rolling back the quantized model on that pool now: `rollout undo ml-serving-3 --revision=previous`
prashant: Rollback completed. Instances are restarting and coming back healthy (no OOMs in latest 3m).
infra-ryan: New gateway pods are up, readiness probes green. No further crashloops observed on gateway.
kevin: Good. Can we monitor for 10 more minutes and then decide if we revert circuit-breakers / weights?
sara: Monitoring window 10m started. Current aggregate 5xx rate at 1.1% and trending down.
ops-oncall: Adding a short-lived synthetic test: `curl -sS -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'` => `200 0.42` on several regions.
support-jess: Sent follow-up to affected customers: short mitigations and expected full resolution in 15–30m.
kevin: I'll hand off to infra-ryan for monitoring and postmortem. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
infra-ryan: Handoff acknowledged. I'll keep an eye on dashboards and open a postmortem doc. Preliminary RCA: quantized model variant caused increased memory/GC pressure on ml-serving-3 → upstream timeouts → elevated 502/504 at edge; contributing factor: single pool had higher traffic weight.
incident-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated. Severity lowered to SEV-2. De-escalating pager.
kevin: Filing follow-up tasks:
• postmortem (assigned to prashant + infra-ryan)
• add automated canary for model mem/latency signals before pool promotion
• increase multi-pool traffic steering to avoid single-point overload
• improve alerting to include upstream GC/OOM signals

prashant: I'll own the canary task and model rollout checklist updates.
infra-ryan: I'll draft the postmortem and share in #postmortems. Will attach timeline and graphs.
sara: Thanks all. Marking thread resolved in 30m if no regressions. :eyes:
